exam.title: 2024年 考研英语(一) 真题

passages.title: Section I: Use of English (完形填空 1-20题·自动门与空间优化)
passages.content:
There's nothing more welcoming than opening a door for you. (1)_______ the need to be touched to open or close, automatic doors are essential in (2)_______ disabled access to buildings and helping provide general (3)_______ to commercial buildings. Self-sliding doors began to emerge as a commercial product in 1960 after being invented six years (4)_______ by two Americans, Dee Horton and Lew Hewitt. They (5)_______ as a novelty feature, but as their use has grown, their (6)_______ have extended within our technologically advanced world. Particularly (7)_______ in busy locations and during times of emergency, the doors (8)_______ crowd management by reducing the obstacles put in people's way. (9)_______ making access both in and out of buildings easier for people, the difference in the way many of these doors open helps to reduce the total area (10)_______ by them.

Automatic doors often open to the side, with the panels sliding across one another. Replacing swing doors, these (11)_______ smaller spaces to maximise the usable space inside without having to (12)_______ the way for a large, sticking-out door. There are many different types of automatic door, with each (13)_______ specific signals to tell them when to open. (14)_______ these methods differ, the main (15)_______ remain the same. Each automatic door system (16)_______ the light, sound, weight, or movement in their vicinity as a signal. Sensor-types are chosen to (17)_______ the different environments they are needed in. (18)_______, a busy road might not (19)_______ a motion-sensored door, as it would constantly be opening for passers-by. A pressure-sensitive mat would be more (20)_______ to limit the surveyed area.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A (Text 1·罗马铁钉与技术经济史)
passages.content:
About 2,000 years ago, as the Roman army abandoned its fortress at Inchtuthil in Perthshire, soldiers buried nearly a million iron nails in a pit, concealing them under 12 feet of gravel. The hoard remained untouched until archaeologists unearthed it in 1960. The Romans had not buried the nails out of superstition; rather, in their hurried retreat, they desperately needed to prevent these critical military-grade iron supplies from falling into the hands of hostile local Caledonian tribes, who coveted iron for weapons.

Nails have long played a pivotal yet underappreciated role in shaping human civilisation. In the early 17th century, nails were so scarce and valuable in the American colonies that settlers in Virginia reportedly burned down their own cabins when moving, simply to recover the precious hand-forged nails from the ashes. Recognising this destructive practice, the Virginia legislature was compelled to pass a statute offering citizens public land and alternative incentives specifically to discourage the burning of private homes for nails.

For millennia, blacksmiths laboured individually over each nail, shaping iron rod by rod with manual hammer blows. Consequently, nail prices remained remarkably high, constituting a substantial portion of any construction project. However, beginning in the late 18th century and accelerating through the Industrial Revolution, the advent of rolling mills, cutting machines, and mechanized wire fabrication triggered unprecedented shifts in nail economics. Increased productivity, accompanied by streamlined supply chains, caused nail prices to plummet dramatically over the subsequent century.

Today, nails have become ubiquitous and virtually free, sold by the kilogram in bulk boxes at hardware superstores. Economists study nails precisely because, while their basic functional form has remained virtually identical from Roman times to the present day, the trajectory of their pricing offers a transparent window into two centuries of industrial growth. Ultimately, the profound lesson of the nail is that civilization is not propelled solely by dazzling, complex machines; cheap, modest technologies can unleash equally revolutionary transformations across human history.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A (Text 2·非洲狩猎采集部落育儿与现代协作育儿)
passages.content:
Parenting tips obtained from hunter-gatherers in Africa may be the key to bringing up more contented children, researchers have suggested. In modern Western societies, raising infants is predominantly framed as an isolated, high-stress endeavor borne almost exclusively by biological mothers and fathers. Yet evolutionary anthropologists observing traditional Mbendjele BaYaka hunter-gatherer communities in the Congo basin observed a starkly different arrangement: child care is distributed across a dynamic, cooperative network of community members, a social practice termed "alloparenting".

In these traditional groups, infants receive attention, comforting, and direct physical care from more than a dozen different caregivers each day, ranging from grandparents and aunts to older siblings and unrelated neighbors. This widespread network buffers mothers from postpartum fatigue and emotional burnout, while ensuring that crying infants are responded to within seconds.

Recognising that modern urban living has dismantled these ancestral support structures, progressive communities in Europe are experimenting with hybrid models. In Germany, experimental multigenerational co-housing schemes deliberately bring young families together with retired senior citizens in shared architectural complexes. The elders provide spontaneous childcare and emotional companionship, while young parents assist seniors with heavy chores and technology, effectively re-establishing an alloparenting ecosystem within a contemporary suburban context.

By contrast, the prevailing "intensive mothering narrative" dominant across industrialized societies places unrealistic moral pressure on nuclear family units, particularly working mothers. By compelling a single caregiver to serve as educator, playmate, protector, and emotional anchor round the clock, this modern narrative departs drastically from the evolutionary trajectory that shaped human psychology. Cross-cultural data reveals that maternal depression and pediatric anxiety disorders are substantially lower in societies with robust communal caregiving.

Early childhood institutions in the UK and North America could benefit immensely from adopting alloparenting principles. Currently, commercial nurseries often suffer from rigid carer-to-child ratios that foster transactional, impersonal environments. Encouraging mixed-age playgroups, involving extended families, and improving staffing ratios would create warmer, evolutionarily aligned environments for child development.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A (Text 3)
passages.content:
In an era dominated by hyper-connected smartphones and omnipresent notification feeds, the concept of the human attention span has emerged as a central cultural anxiety. Commentators routinely lament that continuous exposure to short-form video snippets and algorithmically personalized feeds has fractured our capacity for sustained contemplation, reducing modern intellects to superficial skimmers incapable of deep literary or philosophical engagement.

However, historical and cognitive perspectives invite a more nuanced interpretation. Historical research demonstrates that societal panic regarding the decay of attention is far from unprecedented. The invention of the printing press in the fifteenth century provoked grave warnings that the deluge of cheap books would overwhelm human memory and breed intellectual indolence. Similarly, the advent of nineteenth-century newspapers and early twentieth-century radio broadcasts was met with moral alarms that readers and listeners were losing the discipline required for scholarly reflection.

Cognitive psychologists point out that attention is not an immutable, single cognitive tank that is drained by novel media; rather, it is a highly malleable behavioral adaptation. Humans dynamically allocate cognitive resources according to ecological demands. While our capacity for prolonged passive immersion may indeed be challenged in fragmented digital environments, users concurrently develop sophisticated scanning and synthesis heuristics that allow them to process vast amounts of disparate information with remarkable velocity.

The urgent challenge, therefore, is not to wage a futile war against digital technologies or retreat into nostalgic technophobia. Instead, educational institutions must foster cognitive agency: the intentional cultivation of metacognitive habits that enable individuals to consciously toggle between rapid information triage and deep, uninterrupted mental focus.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A (Text 4)
passages.content:
Major municipal art museums across Europe and North America are navigating a precarious fiscal landscape. Traditionally reliant on a tripartite funding model composed of governmental grants, corporate philanthropy, and private benefactors, these esteemed cultural institutions have found their balance sheets severely battered by persistent post-pandemic visitor hesitation, galloping inflation, and escalating energy overheads.

Faced with declining operational subsidies, several premier galleries have instituted steep ticket price increases, pushing general admission past the thirty-dollar mark. While museum directors defend these price adjustments as inevitable measures to keep gallery lights illuminated and safeguard irreplaceable cultural treasures, social equity advocates protest that exorbitant fees transform public cultural sanctuaries into exclusionary clubs reserved exclusively for affluent patrons.

Simultaneously, the ethics of cultural philanthropy have undergone intense public scrutiny. Grassroots activist groups and museum employees have mounted sustained campaigns demanding that institutions sever ties with corporate sponsors linked to fossil fuel extraction, arms manufacturing, or controversial pharmaceutical conglomerates. When institutions bow to public pressure and decline disreputable endowments, however, they rarely find alternative philanthropists ready to fill the resulting budgetary chasms.

In response to this multi-front squeeze, progressive museum administrators are re-evaluating their core operating paradigms. Instead of staging prohibitively expensive, international blockbusters that require exorbitant insurance and freight fees, galleries are leaning into their permanent collections, creating inventive thematic juxtapositions and digital narrative experiences that resonate with localized audiences without incurring ruinous debt.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part B (新题型 41-45题)
passages.content:
The emergence of autonomous artificial agents capable of reasoning, synthesizing empirical literature, and formulating hypotheses is initiating a paradigm shift in the scientific method. Traditionally, scientific discoveries were generated through a hypothesis-driven process formulated solely by human intellect.

[41] ____________________________________________________________________

Automated laboratory platforms can run tens of thousands of experimental variations per day, testing chemical reactions or genomic alterations with precision that far exceeds human capabilities. However, data generation alone does not constitute scientific understanding.

[42] ____________________________________________________________________

This epistemic asymmetry poses profound dilemmas for peer review and scientific verification. If an artificial intelligence identifies a novel molecular compound capable of curing an aggressive pathogen, but human biochemists cannot retrace the generative logic behind the discovery, should the treatment be authorized for clinical trials?

[43] ____________________________________________________________________

Furthermore, scientific mentorship and serendipitous insight risk degradation if doctoral candidates are reduced to passive technicians who merely execute machine-generated research directives.

[44] ____________________________________________________________________

To safeguard scientific integrity, leading research universities and international academies are establishing 'human-in-the-loop' governance charters. Under these frameworks, algorithmic tools must provide verifiable provenance for every claim, and human co-authors remain legally accountable for methodological rigor.

[45] ____________________________________________________________________

Ultimately, artificial intelligence should be embraced not as an autonomous oracle that supplants human scientists, but as an intellectual telescope that expands our capacity to illuminate natural mysteries.

questions.stem: Choose the best option for (1) in the text:

options.text: Through
Despite
Besides
Without

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】介词语义辨析。句意：无需触碰即可开关，自动门对于改善残障人士通行至关重要。此处表达'无需接触'，故选 Without。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for (2) in the text:

options.text: revealing
demanding
improving
tracing

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】动宾搭配。improve access to... 为固定搭配，表示'改善进入/通达的便利性'。C符合语境。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for (3) in the text:

options.text: experience
convenience
guidance
reference

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】名词语义。自动门为商业建筑提供普遍的'便利'（convenience），与前文 disabled access 并列呼应。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for (4) in the text:

options.text: previously
temporarily
successively
eventually

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】时间副词。表示在1960年成为商品化产品的'六年前'（即1954年）已被发明，选 previously。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for (5) in the text:

options.text: held on
started out
settled down
went by

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】动词短语。start out as 表示'起初作为……出现'，后文 but 提示从新奇特征向普及效益转变。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for (6) in the text:

options.text: threats
concerns
benefits
origins

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】名词辨析。随着使用量激增，自动门的益处/好处（benefits）在现代社会进一步拓展。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for (7) in the text:

options.text: useful
flexible
stable
common

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】形容词辨析。在繁忙人流场所与紧急疏散时刻，自动门尤其'实用'（useful）。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for (8) in the text:

options.text: call for
yield to
look into
act as

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】动词短语。act as crowd management 表示自动门通过消除障碍'充当/起到人群疏导管理'的作用。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for (9) in the text:

options.text: As well as
In terms of
In addition to
In place of

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】逻辑连接短语。As well as making access...，表示'不仅使人们进出建筑物更加容易，而且……'，引导并列增补关系。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for (10) in the text:

options.text: connected
shared
defended
occupied

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】后置定语动词。平移门相比传统推拉门，有助于缩减门扇自身所'占据'（occupied）的总空间面积。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for (11) in the text:

options.text: allow
expect
require
direct

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】动词句型。allow smaller spaces to maximise...，allow sb/sth to do 表示'使得狭小空间得以最大化内部可用空间'。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for (12) in the text:

options.text: adopt
lead
clear
change

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】动宾搭配。clear the way 为固定成语搭配，意为'为……腾出/扫清道路'，不必为向外突出的笨重大门腾出回转通道。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for (13) in the text:

options.text: adapting to
deriving from
relying on
pointing at

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】介词短语。rely on specific signals 意为'依赖特定信号'来提示其开启动作。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for (14) in the text:

options.text: Once
Since
Unless
Although

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】让步状语从句。Although these methods differ, the main principles remain the same. 尽管传感方式各异，但核心机理一致。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for (15) in the text:

options.text: positions
restrictions
principles
categories

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】名词语义。main principles remain the same，指自动门运作的基本'物理原则/原理'保持不变。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for (16) in the text:

options.text: controls
analyses
predicts
produces

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】动词搭配。自动门系统将周围环境中的光线、声音或重力变动作信号进行'分析'（analyses）。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for (17) in the text:

options.text: decorate
ignore
establish
match

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】动词搭配。传感器类型的选择是为了与所需的实际应用环境相'匹配'（match the different environments）。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for (18) in the text:

options.text: In contrast
By comparison
For example
Above all

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】逻辑过渡词。后文以繁华路段马路边不适合红外移动传感器为例进行举例说明，故用 For example。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for (19) in the text:

options.text: assess
suit
protect
identify

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】动宾语义。繁忙路段可能不'适合'（suit）微波移动感应门，否则会对每一个路人频繁误开。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for (20) in the text:

options.text: appropriate
sensitive
accessible
accurate

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】形容词辨析。在此类临街场景下，压力感应地垫更加'合适/恰当'（appropriate），可严格限制感应区域。

questions.stem: The Romans buried the nails probably for the sake of ______.

options.text: saving them for future use.
keeping them from rusting.
letting them grow in value.
hiding them from the locals.

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】细节事实题。第一段末句明确指出：'they desperately needed to prevent these critical military-grade iron supplies from falling into the hands of hostile local Caledonian tribes'（急需防止关键铁料落入当地卡利多尼部落之手），对应 D 项 hiding them from the locals（向当地人隐匿掩埋）。

questions.stem: The example of early 17th-century Virginians is used to ______.

options.text: highlight the thriftiness of early American colonists.
illustrate the high status of blacksmiths in that period.
contrast the attitudes of different civilisations toward nails.
show the preciousness of nail-making technology at that time.

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】例证题。第二段以17世纪弗吉尼亚殖民者甚至烧毁房屋来回收手工铁钉为例，正是为了论证前一句'nails were so scarce and valuable'，彰显当时制钉材料与手工制钉技术的极其珍贵稀缺，选 D。

questions.stem: What played the major role in lowering the price of nails after the late 1700s?

options.text: Increased productivity.
Wider use of new energies.
Fiercer market competition.
Reduced cost of raw materials.

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】因果细节题。第三段指出，轧钢机与机械化拉丝制钉机的问世带来了'Increased productivity'（生产力的极大提升），直接推动铁钉价格发生断崖式下跌，A 为原文对应核心词。

questions.stem: It can be learned from Paragraph 5 that nails ______.

options.text: have undergone many technological improvements.
have remained basically the same since Roman times.
are less studied than other everyday products.
are one of the world's most significant inventions.

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】细节判断题。末段指出：'their basic functional form has remained virtually identical from Roman times to the present day'（其基本物理功能形态自罗马时代至今几乎完全相同），与 B 项 have remained basically the same 语义完全一致。

questions.stem: Which of the following best summarizes the last two paragraphs?

options.text: Cheap technologies bring about revolutionary change.
Technological innovation is integral to economic success.
Technology defines people's understanding of the world.
Sophisticated technology developed from small inventions.

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】段落主旨概括题。文章末尾总结指出：'civilization is not propelled solely by dazzling, complex machines; cheap, modest technologies can unleash equally revolutionary transformations'（文明不仅仅由昂贵复杂机器推动，廉价朴素的技术同样能掀起革命性变革），A 项完美概括全文主旨。

questions.stem: According to the first two paragraphs, alloparenting refers to the practice of ______.

options.text: sharing child care among community members.
assigning babies to specific adult caregivers.
teaching parenting details to older children.
carrying infants around by their parent.

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】词义理解题。第一段末指出：'child care is distributed across a dynamic, cooperative network of community members, a social practice termed "alloparenting"'，表明协作育儿是指在社区成员之间共同分担育儿照护，选 A。

questions.stem: The scheme in Germany is mentioned to illustrate ______.

options.text: an attempt to facilitate intergenerational communication.
an approach to integrating alloparenting into western culture.
the conventional parenting style in western culture.
the differences between western and African ways of living.

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】例证题。第三段通过德国多代同堂共居社区将年轻家庭与退休长者结合的案例，旨在说明如何将原始'协作育儿'理念融入现代西方生活方式，选 B。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 4, the "intensive mothering narrative" ______.

options.text: alleviate parenting pressure.
considerate family relationships.
results in the child-centered family.
departs from the course of evolution.

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】细节事实题。第四段明确指出：'this modern narrative departs drastically from the evolutionary trajectory that shaped human psychology'，强调密集育儿观念与人类心理形成的历史演化轨迹相背离，选 D。

questions.stem: According to paragraph 5, what can we learn about nurseries in the UK?

options.text: They tend to fall short of official requirements.
They have difficulty finding enough caregivers.
They ought to improve their carer-to-child ratio.
They should try to prevent parental depression.

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】细节推断题。末段指出托儿所目前因刻板的师生比而导致冷漠机械化，建议'improving staffing ratios would create warmer, evolutionarily aligned environments'，即英国幼托机构应当优化改善师幼配比，选 C。

questions.stem: Which of the following would be the best title for the text?

options.text: Instructive teaching: a dilemma for anxious parents.
For a happier family, learn from the hunter-gatherers.
Mix-aged playgroup, a better choice for lonely children.
Tracing the history of parenting: from Africa to Europe.

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】主旨标题题。文章首尾呼应，开篇立论向非洲狩猎采集部落取经，探讨现代家庭如何摆脱密集育儿焦虑，建立快乐和谐的育儿协作网络，B 选项概括最生动精准。

questions.stem: Cultural commentators commonly worry that digital media has ______.

options.text: undermined human capacity for sustained and deep contemplation
diminished youth engagement with democratic politics
completely replaced formal classroom instruction
caused permanent physical deterioration of ocular vision

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】细节事实题。第一段指出评论家担心短视频与算法信息流击碎了人类持续沉思的能力（fractured our capacity for sustained contemplation），选 A。

questions.stem: Why does the author mention the printing press and nineteenth-century newspapers in Paragraph 2?

options.text: To demonstrate that modern attention anxiety has historical precedents
To argue that historical media technologies were strictly superior
To praise the early moralists for their farsightedness
To urge the modern press to return to vintage typesetting

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】例证修辞目的题。作者在第二段列举印刷术和报纸的恐慌史，旨在说明针对注意力衰退的社会恐慌自古有之、并非史无前例（far from unprecedented），选 A。

questions.stem: According to cognitive psychologists, human attention is ______.

options.text: a rigid biological faculty that cannot be trained
an adaptable behavior that responds dynamically to environmental demands
wholly superior when consuming printed books over screens
permanently extinguished by short-form video consumption

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】细节事实题。第三段指出注意力并非一成不变的蓄水池，而是一种高度可塑的行为适应能力（highly malleable behavioral adaptation），根据环境需求动态调配，选 B。

questions.stem: What do modern users develop while navigating digital environments?

options.text: An inability to synthesize any textual information
Advanced heuristics for rapid scanning and synthesizing disparate information
A strict psychological aversion toward electronic communication
Enhanced photographic memory for ancient scripts

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】细节事实题。第三段末句指出数字环境中的用户发展出了快速扫读和综合归纳复杂信息的启发式技能（sophisticated scanning and synthesis heuristics），选 B。

questions.stem: The author concludes that educational institutions should ______.

options.text: ban smartphones entirely from all campus grounds
cultivate students' metacognitive ability to toggle between focus modes
replace traditional books exclusively with digital tablets
discourage philosophical reading in favor of coding skills

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】作者观点与结论题。第四段指出教育机构不应退回技术恐惧症，而应培养认知自主性（cognitive agency），让学生能在快速初筛与深度专注之间自如切换，选 B。

questions.stem: Which factor has contributed to the fiscal distress of municipal art museums?

options.text: Surging inflation and escalating energy expenditures
A total boycott by local educational school districts
Legal restrictions on purchasing international artifacts
Mandatory quotas on displaying digital NFT artworks

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】细节事实题。第一段末尾指出博物馆财政受到访客观望、恶性通胀及能源支出激增的沉重打击（galloping inflation, and escalating energy overheads），选 A。

questions.stem: Critics argue that raising museum admission prices will ______.

options.text: permanently eliminate the need for philanthropic donations
alienate less affluent visitors and foster cultural exclusion
force museums to sell off core national collections
hasten the deterioration of delicate historical canvases

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】细节推断题。第二段指出高票价将公共文化殿堂变为了唯富人专享的排他性俱乐部（exclusionary clubs reserved exclusively for affluent patrons），选 B。

questions.stem: Why does severing ties with controversial corporate donors create difficulties for museums?

options.text: It violates binding international copyright treaties
It rarely results in finding alternative donors to fill the financial void
It triggers immediate revocation of museum operating licenses
It prompts employee strikes across all curatorial departments

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】因果细节题。第三段末句阐明拒绝声誉不佳的捐赠后，很难找到替代资助者填补预算鸿沟（rarely find alternative philanthropists ready to fill the resulting budgetary chasms），选 B。

questions.stem: How are progressive museums adapting to the budgetary squeeze?

options.text: By staging even more lavish international blockbuster spectacles
By creatively leveraging permanent collections for localized audiences
By auctioning off public masterpieces to private hedge funds
By transferring all operations into proprietary virtual reality metaverses

questions.explanation: 【考点精析】细节事实题。第四段指出美术馆放弃烧钱的国际巡展，而是深挖馆藏常设展（leaning into their permanent collections），创造共鸣且低负债的策展体验，选 B。

questions.stem: Which of the following would be the best title for the text?

options.text: The Disappearance of Fine Art in Contemporary Society
Municipal Museums: Financial Crises, Ethical Dilemmas, and Strategic Shifts
